assumptions: full-space operator norm bounds; not merely probe residuals
theorems.cost: d-1 B actions to form candidate plus1 original-residual action; O(dN) when B action O(N)
theorems.proof: synthetic division; (I-B)p(B) identity; inverse Neumann bound for I-q(B)/q(1)
limitations: floating implementation is not outward-rounded certification
setup/witness construction cost not included in action count

theorems.statement: For constant A=-kappa I+omega R with R^2=-I, y(t+h)=exp(hA)y(t)+h phi1(hA)b for constant b; entire phi1 removes singularity at A=0.
theorems.cost: O(N) per action with fixed block representation
theorems.proof: variation of constants and entire-function identity
limitations: roundoff and phase argument reduction are implementation concerns

theorems.statement: For c cos(nu t)+d sin(nu t), forcing action is sum over sigma=+-1 of exp(i sigma nu(t+h))*h*phi1(h(A-i sigma nu I))*c_sigma, c_sigma=(c-i sigma d)/2.
assumptions: For O(N) code cost: same declared fixed2x2 damped-rotation block representation as T-AFFINE
Implementation requires finite represented phase and shifted frequencies
theorems.proof: complex harmonic decomposition and variation of constants; phi1(0)=1 covers resonance
limitations: endpoint action, not a general nonlinear harmonic solver wrapper

theorems.statement: For fixed weighted-self-adjoint nonpositive Q, s>=2 and h Lambda<=(s*s+s-2)/2, RKL2 is W-contractive and global error<=5*T*h_max^2*||Q^3 y0||_W/18.
assumptions: positive cell weights and symmetric nonnegative conductances
all time steps satisfy stable interval
theorems.cost: O(E*T/h + E*T*sqrt(Lambda/h)) at fixed accuracy step h; accuracy-independent grid scaling additionally requires uniformly bounded ||Q^3y0||_W
theorems.proof: Legendre derivative bound, Taylor remainder<=5x^3/18, spectral calculus and telescoping contraction
limitations: not a theorem for general nonlinear/nonnormal PDE

theorems.statement: For stochastic P=I+Q/q, q>0, normalized nonnegative truncated Poisson weights preserve positivity/mass and propagator error is at most2*tau in a Markov contraction norm. Q=0 uses identity.
assumptions: fixed Markov generator with invariant weights
tau is true omitted probability mass
theorems.cost: implemented splitting uses h*q<=32 per chunk; total cost may grow with polar q
theorems.proof: bound omitted tail by tau and normalization perturbation by tau, then telescope contractions
limitations: no unconditional improvement over Euler or RKL2

theorems.statement: Pilot attempts<=min(global attempt budget,pilot_limit*pilot_attempt_budget). For stationary equal-accuracy per-interval ratio r=implicit/explicit<1, one replay pays back after K>r/(1-r) future intervals.
assumptions: comparable achieved accuracy and stationary costs for payoff inequality
theorems.cost: finite work cap, not callback wall-time bound
limitations: nonstationary stiffness can violate payoff assumptions

theorems.statement: Continuous one-sided growth plus residual/spatial defects and remap jumps yields Gamma-weighted error accumulation; positive conservative remap is contractive in weighted L1.
assumptions: one-sided growth bound on relevant error segments
remap consistency and numerical perturbations separately bounded
no double counting of approximate flow defect
theorems.cost: permits explicit cumulative error budget; not a wall-time theorem
theorems.proof: Dini differential inequality, integrating factor, remap Lipschitz recursion; |Rz|<=R|z|
limitations: budget checks are exact small examples, not physical PDE bound certification
preserving mass alone does not preserve solution accuracy

distinction: Conditional analytic bounds are not measured timing guarantees or floating-point interval certificates.
